question: Find the greatest number that will divide 49, 97 and 189 so as to leave the same remainder in each case.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The greatest number leaving the same remainder is the HCF of the differences between the given numbers.

Given numbers are 49, 97, and 189.

Differences = |97 − 49|, |189 − 97|, and |189 − 49|.

The differences are 48, 92, and 140.

HCF(48, 92, 140) = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 49, 97, and 189.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = HCF of (y − x), (z − y), and (z − x) where x [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF for Same Remainder

When a number divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder, the greatest such number is the HCF of the absolute differences: |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

HCF for Specific Remainders

When a number divides x, y, and z leaving specific remainders a, b, and c respectively, the greatest such number is the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

LCM with Specific Remainder

The smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder r in each case is obtained by finding LCM(x, y, z) + r.
